data.title: Company Valuation
data.statement:
Estimate a company's value from its historical annual profits.

For each of [[k]] consecutive years, you know [[profitBeforeTax]] and [[taxes]]. [[profitBeforeTax]] is the company's profit after operating costs, including salaries, but before taxes. The statements are ordered from oldest to newest.

Calculate each historical <<net income>> as [[profitBeforeTax]] - [[taxes]]. Fit a straight line to the historical net incomes using <<ordinary least squares with a free intercept>>. Use the line to forecast [[n]] years and capitalize their average income.

The current year is the first year without a statement and the first of the [[n]] forecast years.

Assign [[x]] = {{1}} to the oldest statement and [[x]] = [[k]] to the latest. Let [[y]] denote a historical net income and [[yₓ]] its value for year [[x]]. Calculate:

[[xMean]] = ([[k]] + {{1}}) / {{2}}
[[yMean]] = arithmetic mean of [[y]] for the [[k]] years

```
        [[k]]
        ∑ ([[x]] - [[xMean]])([[yₓ]] - [[yMean]])
      [[x]]=1
[[m]] = ————————————————————————————————
        [[k]]
        ∑ ([[x]] - [[xMean]])²
      [[x]]=1
```

[[q]] = [[yMean]] - [[m]] × [[xMean]]
[[forecast]]([[x]]) = [[m]] × [[x]] + [[q]]

Forecast [[x]] = [[k]] + {{1}}, [[k]] + {{2}}, …, [[k]] + [[n]]. The first forecast ([[k]] + {{1}}) is the current-year income.

[[averageForecastIncome]] = arithmetic mean of the [[n]] forecast incomes
[[companyValue]] = [[averageForecastIncome]] / [[capitalizationRate]]

The capitalization rate is supplied as a decimal: {{0.10}} means {{10%}}.

<<Do not round intermediate calculations.>> Format the final values as described in the Output section. Negative forecasts and negative company values are valid results of this simplified model; do not replace them with zero.

This is an educational model. The capitalization rate is an assumption, and a linear trend may produce economically unrealistic forecasts.

STATEMENT
Use the historical net incomes to forecast future income and estimate the company's value.

INPUT
k: Number of historical statements, ordered from oldest to newest.
n: Number of forecast years, including the current year.
capitalizationRate: Decimal capitalization rate; 0.10 means 10 percent.
profitBeforeTax: Company profit after operating costs, before taxes.
taxes: Company taxes for this historical year.

OUTPUT
Print historical net incomes, forecast incomes, their average, and company value on four lines, with two decimal places.
data.inputDescription:

<<Next [[k]] lines:>> two integers [[profitBeforeTax]] and [[taxes]], separated by a single space, for one historical annual statement, from oldest to newest. All monetary inputs use the same currency unit.
data.outputDescription:
<<Line 1:>> [[k]] historical net incomes, from oldest to newest, separated by single spaces.
<<Line 2:>> [[n]] forecast incomes, starting with the current year, separated by single spaces.
<<Line 3:>> [[averageForecastIncome]].
<<Line 4:>> [[companyValue]].

Print every monetary value with exactly {{2}} digits after the decimal point. Use a dot as the decimal separator, without currency symbols or thousands separators.

Round each final value independently to the nearest hundredth. If a value is exactly halfway between two hundredths, round away from zero: {{3.125}} becomes {{3.13}} and {{-3.125}} becomes {{-3.13}}. Print zero as {{0.00}}, never {{-0.00}}.

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

Estimate a company's value from its historical annual profits.

For each of k consecutive years, you know profitBeforeTax and taxes. profitBeforeTax is the company's profit after operating costs, including salaries, but before taxes. The statements are ordered from oldest to newest.

Calculate each historical net income as profitBeforeTax - taxes. Fit a straight line to the historical net incomes using ordinary least squares with a free intercept. Use the line to forecast n years and capitalize their average income.

The current year is the first year without a statement and the first of the n forecast years.

Assign x = 1 to the oldest statement and x = k to the latest. Let y denote a historical net income and yₓ its value for year x. Calculate:

xMean = (k + 1) / 2
yMean = arithmetic mean of y for the k years


        k
        ∑ (x - xMean)(yₓ - yMean)
      x=1
m = ————————————————————————————————
        k
        ∑ (x - xMean)²
      x=1


q = yMean - m × xMean
forecast(x) = m × x + q

Forecast x = k + 1, k + 2, …, k + n. The first forecast (k + 1) is the current-year income.

averageForecastIncome = arithmetic mean of the n forecast incomes
companyValue = averageForecastIncome / capitalizationRate

The capitalization rate is supplied as a decimal: 0.10 means 10%.

Do not round intermediate calculations. Format the final values as described in the Output section. Negative forecasts and negative company values are valid results of this simplified model; do not replace them with zero.

This is an educational model. The capitalization rate is an assumption, and a linear trend may produce economically unrealistic forecasts.




   

      
Input

      
Line 1: two integers k, the number of historical statements, and n, the number of forecast years including the current year, followed by a decimal capitalizationRate, separated by single spaces.

Next k lines: two integers profitBeforeTax and taxes, separated by a single space, for one historical annual statement, from oldest to newest. All monetary inputs use the same currency unit.

   

   

      
Output

      
Line 1: k historical net incomes, from oldest to newest, separated by single spaces.
Line 2: n forecast incomes, starting with the current year, separated by single spaces.
Line 3: averageForecastIncome.
Line 4: companyValue.

Print every monetary value with exactly 2 digits after the decimal point. Use a dot as the decimal separator, without currency symbols or thousands separators.

Round each final value independently to the nearest hundredth. If a value is exactly halfway between two hundredths, round away from zero: 3.125 becomes 3.13 and -3.125 becomes -3.13. Print zero as 0.00, never -0.00.

   

   

      
Constraints

      
5 ≤ k ≤ 10
1 ≤ n ≤ 10
0.0001 ≤ capitalizationRate ≤ 1
capitalizationRate uses ordinary decimal notation with at most 4 digits after the decimal point.
0 ≤ profitBeforeTax ≤ 10⁶
0 ≤ taxes ≤ profitBeforeTax

   

   

      
Example

      

         

            
Input

            
5 1 0.20
12 2
24 4
36 6
48 8
60 10

         

         

            
Output

            
10.00 20.00 30.00 40.00 50.00
60.00
60.00
300.00
